role: Precision-timing detector expert, FCC / muon-collider detector R&D selection panel
assessment: The timing case rests on the DSB:Ce capillary channel: ref-included median trend 323/sqrt(E) (+) 79 ps over six points (Output/scan_dsb1/EnergyScanDSB1.png; FINDINGS.md lines 548-575), and quoted intrinsic values ~145/137 ps at 5/7 GeV and ~75 ps at 9 GeV after subtracting the diagonal-difference-validated ~110 ps reference (FINDINGS.md lines 659-673; Output/summary/DiagDiff_DSB1.txt, DiagDiff_LuAG.txt). Against requirements: FCC-hh pileup vertexing at 5-10 ps/track is not this technology's regime and should not be the metric — that spec belongs to dedicated MIP timing layers (CMS MTD BTL achieves 30-60 ps/MIP with LYSO+SiPM as the field precedent). The correct FCC-hh question is high-energy EM shower time-stamping (H->gg vertexing class, ~30 ps at >=50 GeV per CMS ECAL precedent). The correct muon-collider question is cell-level BIB rejection at ~30-60 ps for few-GeV deposits (CRILIN precedent ~20-45 ps at 0.5-1 GeV). NEW finding 1 (major, favorable): the published intrinsic ladder 145/137/75 ps mixes estimators — 145/137 derive from the MEAN-combination included widths (182.1/176.0 ps in DiagDiff_DSB1.txt) while 75 derives from the MEDIAN width (133 ps); recomputing a median-consistent ladder from the scan medians (156/140/133 ps at 5/7/9, minus 110 ps) gives ~111/87/75 ps, which fits a nearly pure-photostatistics ~250/sqrt(E) with no resolved constant term. Extrapolated: ~50 ps at 25 GeV, ~35 ps at 50 GeV, ~25 ps at 100 GeV, plus an intrinsic constant term the 1-9 GeV data cannot resolve (bounded only at <~75 ps). NEW finding 2 (major, unfavorable): the fitted ref-included constant term (79 ps) sits BELOW the validated 107-114 ps per-event reference floor — the two-parameter fit predicts 107 ps total already at 20 GeV, i.e. below the reference alone. The b=79 ps trend is unphysical outside the fitted range and must not be quoted as a constant term; only the ref-subtracted per-point ladder is meaningful. Verified in macros/BestTiming.C lines 158-170: capillaries and TR0 copy are timed in the same DRS4 group against tax[1], so the ~110 ps common mode is the irreducible DT5742+MCP digitization floor of THIS setup, not an analysis inefficiency — with sigma_meas only ~1.2x sigma_ref at 9 GeV, every intrinsic number is a quadrature subtraction of near-equal quantities (75 ps carries ~+/-10 ps from the 133+/-5 measurement plus ~+/-5 ps per +/-3.5 ps of reference uncertainty, before the run-15->22 MCP HV drop, which makes porting the LuAG-validated reference to DSB1 runs 31-38 an untested assumption). Structure verdict: the sqrt(E) (+) constant form is favorable — the constant term halved (138->79 ps ref-included) purely by swapping the light-collection channel, and the diagonal-difference discovery of correlated capillary timing in the high-light channel (DiagDiff_DSB1.txt implied_ref = -1 at 5/7/11 GeV) identifies the physics floor (shared shower-depth/position fluctuations) that will not average down with more fibers. Extrapolation to towers: 14x14 mm cells already match muon-collider ECAL granularity; shower-max capillary sampling carries over per cell, but the uncorrected 400-vs-600 ps left/right-column position dependence at 11 GeV (FINDINGS.md lines 450-455) and Longo shower-max migration must be absorbed by a position/depth correction that no tracker existed to demonstrate. LuAG (389/sqrt(E) (+) 138; intrinsic 226/187/183 ps) is a rad-hard fallback, not the timing case; EJ199 is compromised (contaminant hypothesis) and photostat-limited at 1360/sqrt(E) — no timing case.
strengths: DSB1 median-consistent intrinsic ladder ~111/87/75 ps at 5/7/9 GeV is compatible with pure photostatistics ~250/sqrt(E) and no resolved constant term - extrapolating to ~25-35 ps at 50-100 GeV, competitive with CMS ECAL/BTL-class precedents if the constant term cooperates (derived from Output/scan_dsb1 medians + DiagDiff 110 ps reference).

Constant term demonstrated to be engineerable, not module-intrinsic: swapping only the light-collection channel halved the ref-included constant term 138->79 ps (LuAG->DSB1) at fixed LYSO:Ce+W shashlik - a clean R&D lever (FINDINGS.md lines 561-575, 628-648).

Self-validating error accounting rare at this TRL: Randy's diagonal-difference estimator independently recovers the known ~105 ps DRS+MCP reference budget on LuAG at 5-9 GeV (implied_ref 106.6-113.7 ps, DiagDiff_LuAG.txt), and correctly reframed diff/2 as an upper bound when it failed on DSB1.

Discovery of correlated per-capillary timing in the high-light channel (DiagDiff_DSB1.txt implied_ref negative at 5/7/11 GeV) - identifies the physics floor for multi-fiber averaging before a full tower is ever built; most groups would have missed this.

Analysis chain is mature and honest: wall-aware srCFD clip recovery, per-event median combination (rescued light-leak periods and 11 GeV edge-hit outliers), per-run MIP calibration, and 11 GeV points correctly open-markered and excluded from claims.

Referencing verified same-DRS-group (BestTiming.C lines 158-170): the ~110 ps floor is the DT5742+MCP electronics, meaning the detector itself is NOT the current bottleneck - a better reference/TDC directly exposes the intrinsic performance already present in the light.
weaknesses: CRITICAL: the flagship 75 ps @ 9 GeV is a quadrature subtraction of near-equal numbers, (133+/-5) (-) (110+/-4) ps, single point, N=847, with the reference validated only on LuAG runs taken BEFORE the run-15->22 MCP HV reduction - it is a ~75+/-10-15 ps claim pending an independent reference, and the campaign itself flags it 'to be confirmed'.

CRITICAL (new, not in FINDINGS.md): the quoted trend constant term 79 ps is below the validated 107-114 ps per-event reference floor - the sigma_t = 323/sqrt(E) (+) 79 ps parameterization is unphysical when extrapolated (predicts less than the reference alone by 20 GeV) and cannot be presented to a review as the technology's constant term; the intrinsic constant term is unresolved (0 to ~75 ps) by 1-9 GeV data.

MAJOR (new): the published intrinsic ladder 145/137/75 ps mixes mean-combination widths (5/7 GeV, from DiagDiff sigma_meanIncl 182/176 ps) with a median width (9 GeV, 133 ps) - estimator-inconsistent; the median-consistent ladder ~111/87/75 ps should replace it, and quadrature subtraction of a Gaussian reference from robust/median width estimators needs justification.

MAJOR: maximum clean energy is 9 GeV (11 GeV halo-compromised, open markers) - the constant term, the single most decision-relevant quantity for both machines, has no lever arm; PS T10 cannot provide it.

MAJOR: no gain/temperature monitoring - +/-15% cross-run SiPM gain ladder, light-leak noise doubling, MIP normalization proven invalid as a monitor; CFD/srCFD thresholds are amplitude-derived, so timing stability at system level is undemonstrated (per-cell calibration strategy absent).

MAJOR: for muon-collider BIB rejection at few-GeV cell deposits the measured numbers miss the 30-60 ps spec by ~2-4x (intrinsic ~145 ps at 5 GeV, ~350 ps at 1 GeV); the case there requires a ~5-10x detected-photon increase or faster light, not just a better reference.

MAJOR: no radiation-hardness timing data this campaign (DSB:Ce glass and capillary path under FCC-hh/muon-collider shower-max doses), no high-rate/occupancy data (spill-rate DAQ only), no tracker for position/timewalk correction (400-vs-600 ps column asymmetry at 11 GeV left uncorrected), lab DRS4 readout with no system-electronics path.

MINOR: energy-response side is position-smearing dominated (sigma/E 18-65%, intrinsic ~10% bounded once) and linearity only within the +/-15% gain envelope - weak collateral support for the energy-dependent timewalk corrections a real system needs.
open_questions: Does 75 ps @ 9 GeV survive an independent downstream reference with <=20-30 ps jitter (second MCP or LGAD telescope, independent TDC), and does the LuAG-validated 110 ps common mode actually apply to the DSB1 runs taken after the MCP HV drop (runs 31-38)?

What is the intrinsic constant term at 20-150 GeV (SPS H2/H4)? Current data bounds it only below ~75 ps; the 79 ps fitted term is unphysical and everything hinges on whether the true value is ~20 ps or ~60 ps.

Is the correlated capillary timing floor discovered in DSB1 shower physics (irreducible, sets the tower-level limit) or geometry/position (correctable with impact-point information)? What is its magnitude vs cell size and capillary count?

Can detected-photon yield at the capillary be raised the ~5-10x needed for 30-60 ps at few-GeV deposits (muon-collider BIB regime), given DSB1 already improved capture 2.1x over LuAG and the LG chain already grazes its 13.6k ADC-eq ceiling at 11 GeV?

What is the per-cell calibration and monitoring architecture (laser/LED pulser, temperature logging, clock distribution) and the system electronics path replacing the DRS4 (whose ~110 ps same-group reference floor currently dominates every measurement)?
Timing under irradiation: DSB:Ce and quartz-capillary light-path performance after shower-max-equivalent doses, and SiPM timing after fluence - entirely unmeasured for the timing observable.
High-rate behavior: SiPM baseline shift, pulse pileup, and srCFD stability at BIB-like or FCC-hh-like occupancy (T10 provided only ~Hz-scale electrons).
Position dependence: with a tracker, how much of the 400-600 ps edge-vs-center spread and the DSB1 correlated term is removed by an impact-position timewalk map?
recommendation: SPLIT VERDICT, both conditional. Muon collider: YES - earns continued R&D investment. The DSB:Ce channel's photostatistics-limited scaling with no resolved constant term, the demonstrated factor-2 constant-term gain from light-collection engineering alone, cell size already at ECAL granularity, and a rad-hard-plausible LYSO+W+capillary architecture make a credible trajectory toward 30-60 ps at cluster level for tens-of-GeV BIB-discrimination deposits; the gap at few-GeV single-cell deposits (~2-4x) is the stated R&D target, not a disqualifier. FCC-hh: QUALIFIED YES as a high-energy EM shower time-stamp (~25-35 ps extrapolated at 50-100 GeV plus unresolved constant term, CMS-ECAL-class if the constant cooperates) - but explicitly NOT fundable as a 5-10 ps/track vertexing technology, and any FCC-hh claim is premature until the constant term is measured where it matters. Gate the next tranche on a milestone beam test: (1) independent downstream timing reference at <=20-30 ps with a non-DRS4 TDC path - this single change converts nearly every existing systematic subtraction into a direct measurement; (2) SPS energies 20-150 GeV to pin the intrinsic constant term (go/no-go: intrinsic <=60 ps demonstrated directly, not by subtraction); (3) tracker or position tagging for timewalk/position maps and to close the correlated-timing question; (4) pulser+temperature monitoring to kill the gain-ladder systematic; (5) a first irradiated-capillary timing point. Before any external review, the collaboration must stop quoting 323/sqrt(E) (+) 79 ps as a constant-term result (it is below the reference floor) and re-derive the intrinsic ladder with a single consistent estimator (~111/87/75 ps, median-based). EJ199 has no timing case pending the contaminant resolution; LuAG continues only as the radiation-hardness fallback line.
